title: Tiered fragmentation mitigator and compact reuse path for paged KV block manager
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: production workloads showed persistent fragmentation in the paged KV block manager under mixed-generation traffic patterns. Fragmentation caused wasted memory, higher allocation latency and unexpectedly high tail latency during heavy continuous-batching workloads. This PR introduces a two-part approach: (1) a lightweight tiered fragmentation mitigator that separates small/short-lived allocation paths from large/sticky blocks, and (2) a compact reuse path that opportunistically coalesces adjacent free runs and exposes contiguous ranges back to the allocator without global pauses. Implementation details: added a 'fast lane' per-worker freelist for sub-page allocations with probabilistic reclaim to avoid long-lived freelist holds; large-block allocations use a separate set of arenas that prioritize locality and avoid interleaving with the fast lane. The compact reuse path runs at allocation-time and as a bounded background task: it attempts in-place fusion of adjacent free spans and rewires free lists with atomic compare-and-swap to keep lock contention low. Pinning behavior was softened via an exponential backoff with jitter on repeated pin failures, plus a short-lived 'lease' to let in-flight KV readers finish while still offering pages for reuse when safe. Scheduler integration: allocation hotpaths now emit lightweight hints used by the serving scheduler to prefer kernels with aligned physical ranges (reduces TLB/PCIe pressure), and prefetch hints for upcoming KV accesses are emitted for continuous-batching flows to reduce blocking during kv cache population. Testing & benchmarks: unit tests and stress harnesses added (kv_frag_stress_test.py and a Rust micro-benchmark). Microbenchmarks: mixed read/write continuous-batch workload shows 18-23% throughput improvement and tail latency drop of ~28th percentile under our internal bench profile. Safety & rollout: feature guarded behind a runtime flag and disabled by default on older Dedicated nodes. Linear/Jira: ENG-1254 tracked the mitigation strategy; SUP-3421 links an incident where fragmentation regressed a customer workload. Release notes attached. Continuous integration: added a stress job to the bench pool and a canary rollout plan for Dedicated customers.

release_notes: Improves paged KV memory utilization and reduces allocation tail latency by introducing tiered arenas and a compact reuse path. Adds adaptive pin backoff to reduce contention and integrates scheduler hints to improve kernel locality. Rollout: gated behind runtime flag; safe canary for Dedicated customers. Impact: up to ~20% throughput improvement and significant tail-latency reductions for mixed continuous-batching workloads.
